recipe.prompt:
Write two parts of a webinar invitation for someone at {{ account.name }}. {{ sender.name | default: 'The host' }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} sends it.

The session (template owners: keep this text in step with the title, agenda and speakers in this template): "Growing volume, not headcount", a live 45-minute session for operations teams at mid-size logistics and manufacturing companies. A time audit of 40 operations teams: median hours per 100 loads for dispatch, billing, exceptions and customer updates. A carrier's year: 28% more loads with the same 60 people, what it centralized, what it left at the terminals, and the one change that failed in the first month. Then live questions. Everyone who registers gets the recording and the slides.

Inputs: account.industry and account.size_band describe the company. account.dossier.summary is our research summary. data.why_now is a recent reason to reach out and may be empty. person.title is the reader's role and may be empty. Use facts from these inputs and from the session text only. Never invent news, numbers, customers, people or results.

Return JSON with two keys:
- why_you: two sentences, at most 300 characters, on why this session was planned with a company like {{ account.name }} in mind. Tie one fact about them, data.why_now if there is one, to what the talks cover, so it reads like the host wrote it after looking them up. Write to "you" or to the company. Never use a first name; the page adds the greeting. No flattery ("love what you're building", "impressive"), no "I noticed", "I saw" or "I came across", no question.
- takeaways: 4 items {lead, detail}, one for each part of the session that matters most to a {{ person.title | default: 'leader' }} at {{ account.name }}. lead is 3 to 8 words, at most 70 characters, naming the thing they take away, like "The time audit as a sheet". detail is one clause, 20 to 160 characters, that continues the lead into one sentence and says how it applies to their role and company, like "you can run on your dispatch and billing teams in a week". Start detail with a lowercase letter and end it with a period. Numbers come only from the session text.

Rules: no em dashes or en dashes. No email addresses or phone numbers. Plain words a person would say out loud to a peer; no marketing words (unlock, seamless, game-changer, cutting-edge, leverage). Never "real" as emphasis.

Pick the time zone to highlight on a webinar page for someone at {{ account.name }} ({{ account.domain }}).

The zones on the page (template owners: keep this list in step with the time strip in this template): Chicago, New York, Los Angeles, London.

Inputs: account.dossier.summary and account.dossier.why_now. Summary: {{ account.dossier.summary | default: 'none' }}. Why now: {{ account.dossier.why_now | default: 'none' }}.

Step 1: find the city of {{ account.name }}'s headquarters, only if the summary or the why now text says it. The domain name, the industry and the company size do not tell you a location. Never guess a city.

Step 2: return JSON with one key, local_zone: the one listed zone that is in the same time zone as that city, written exactly as listed. Dallas gives "Chicago", Boston gives "New York", Seattle gives "Los Angeles", Manchester gives "London". If the city is not stated, or no listed zone shares its time zone, return an empty string.

recipe.rubric:
Grade the two pieces of copy the way the invited person reads them, on a page for a live session. 10 is copy that reads like the host wrote it after looking the person up and makes the session feel made for them.
Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- specific: why_you ties one real fact about {{ account.name }} to what the talks cover. Generic reasons that would fit any company fail this check.
- fit: each takeaway is something the person can use in their own role at {{ account.name }}, and each one comes from a part of the session.
- plain: short sentences, plain words, no pitch and no flattery.
Answer yes or no:
- grounded: does every fact about {{ account.name }} come from the inputs below?
Automatic fail: an em dash or en dash, a number that is neither in the inputs nor in the session text, an email address or phone number, or a first name in why_you.
Inputs: {{ account.industry | default: 'no industry' }}, {{ account.size_band | default: 'no size' }}. {{ account.dossier.summary | default: 'No summary.' }} Why now: {{ data.why_now | default: 'none' }}. Reader's role: {{ person.title | default: 'not given' }}.
Pass when the overall score is 7.5 or higher, no 0 to 10 check is 6 or lower, and grounded is yes. On a fail, name the check and quote the phrase to change. The fix never supplies replacement facts, names, numbers or results.
